claim: In the large-population household branching model with path-shaped households and independent within-household edge transmission probability \(p=1/2\), the laws \(q^A_1=q^A_3=1/2\) and \(q^B_1=1/3,q^B_2=1/2,q^B_4=1/6\) have the same household-size mean \(2\) and variance \(1\), but for every external-infection mean \(\beta\in(8/13,48/77)\) they straddle the invasion threshold: \(\mathcal R_*^A=13\beta/8>1\) and \(\mathcal R_*^B=77\beta/48<1\). In particular, at \(\beta=31/50\), the exact values are \(403/400\) and \(2387/2400\).

correctness.rationale: For each \(m\), \(H_m\) is obtained by summing indicators that the unique path from the seed to a target has all \(d\) edges open. The exact values \(H_1=1,\ H_2=3/2,\ H_3=11/6,\ H_4=33/16\) yield \(\mathbb E_A[M H_M]=13/4\) and \(\mathbb E_B[M H_M]=77/24\). Both laws have mean 2 and second moment 5. The size-biased household branching mean is \(\beta\,\mathbb E[M H_M]/\mathbb E[M]\), so \(\mathcal R_*^A=13\beta/8\) and \(\mathcal R_*^B=77\beta/48\). They straddle one for \(\beta\in(8/13,48/77)\); at \(\beta=31/50\) the exact values are 403/400 and 2387/2400. No finite experiment is used as proof; the computations are finite exact sums.

evidence: Ball, Sirl, and Trapman, arXiv:0812.4110, Sections 2 and 4.1: a household-level branching process is used, with equal-size households for the main model and per-pair within-household contacts.
Fransson and Trapman, arXiv:1802.05011, Sections 1–3: epidemics on clustered random graphs are analyzed using a branching-process/percolation framework, with clustering represented by triangles.
The inspected Barlow et al. model uses complete mixing within households rather than a path contact graph.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The wider literature establishes that local contact structure and household epidemic size matter, but the inspected statements do not imply the two explicit laws \(q^A\) and \(q^B\) with identical first two moments and opposite invasion classifications. This is a model-specific counterexample, not a claim that prior household-network work ignored topology.

value.rationale: The exact pair is motivated by epidemic invasion classification: a summary using only mean and variance would treat the two household-size laws as identical, while the stated path-transmission model places them on opposite sides of the branching threshold throughout the nonempty interval \(\beta\in(8/13,48/77)\). The value is a qualitative, exact boundary example showing when contact topology/full household-size information matters; it is not a claim that the small numeric gap at \(\beta=31/50\) alone has broad empirical significance.
